dossier.public_summary: The 1% dip repeats every 1.02 days with a V shape and a grazing impact parameter, and centroiding puts it on the target. A second eclipse about 0.76 x as deep as the first and a large phase-curve swing at ~70% of the dip depth show a stellar eclipsing binary, not a planet. The period matching the star's 1.02 d rotation confirms a close binary system.

reasons.why: A second dip at phase 0.7556 with 77% the depth of the primary, far above brightenings, is the signature of a stellar eclipsing binary. A transiting planet cannot produce a 1.2% eclipse of this size on a 1.02 d orbit.
Large out-of-eclipse modulation at 0.7x the transit depth with very high chi2 indicates ellipsoidal/beaming or spot variation from a close binary, not a planet.
V-shaped ingress/egress with grazing impact parameter and large stellar-density mismatch favours total stellar eclipse over planetary transit.
Dip period is essentially identical to measured 1.02 d rotation period with 2.6% spot amplitude; with secondary and V shape this supports synchronous close binary rather than coincidence.
On-target centroid rules out a distant blended neighbour; the eclipsing binary must be on the target itself.
